title: Manual Cell Counting
author: Aparna Kumar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5zng75e

steps.title: Prepare Cell Sample
steps.instruction: Remove 10 µL of the solution containing single cells using a p20 micropipette and transfer to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube or onto a piece of parafilm.

steps.title: Prepare Trypan Blue
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Trypan Blue and use a p20 micropipette to remove 10 µL from the top of the liquid to avoid collecting debris.

steps.title: Stain Cells
steps.instruction: Add the 10 µL of Trypan Blue to the 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube or parafilm containing the cells and gently mix by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Prepare Hemocytometer
steps.instruction: Wipe the hemocytometer and a matching coverslip with 70% ethanol and place them in the biosafety cabinet. Place the coverslip onto the center of the hemocytometer.

steps.title: Load Hemocytometer Chambers
steps.instruction: Load the cell solution into both chambers of the hemocytometer using a p20 micropipette.

substeps.instruction: Remove 10 µL of solution from the tube or parafilm.
Place the pipette tip at the bottom edge of the coverslip and slowly pipette the solution into the bottom chamber until filled.
Remove another 10 µL of solution and place the pipette tip at the top edge of the coverslip to slowly pipette the solution into the top chamber.

steps.title: Focus Microscope
steps.instruction: Place the filled hemocytometer on a microscope and focus until the cells and grid lines in each chamber are clearly visible.

steps.title: Count Cells in Top Grid
steps.instruction: Count cells in 5 different boxes within the top grid (top chamber) using a tally counter.

substeps.instruction: Pick one of the 9 boxes to begin counting.
Count cells on the bottom and right edge lines; do not count cells overlapping the top and left edges.
Note that blue-stained cells are dead and should only be counted for viability, not for the total cell count.
Note the total cells in the box and reset the counter.
Repeat this process for four more boxes in the same grid.

steps.title: Count Cells in Bottom Grid
steps.instruction: Repeat the counting process for the bottom grid (bottom chamber), counting cells in 5 boxes and noting the counts.

steps.title: Calculate Cell Concentration
steps.instruction: Calculate the total number of cells per mL in the original solution.

substeps.instruction: Find the average number of cells per box by adding the total number of cells from all 10 boxes (5 top, 5 bottom) and dividing by 10.
Multiply this average by 2 and then by 10,000.

steps.title: Calculate Total Cells and Viability
steps.instruction: Determine the total cell quantity and the percentage of viable cells using the following formulas:

substeps.instruction: Total number of cells = (number of cells per mL) * (mL of original solution containing the cells)
Cell viability = 100 * (Live cells) / (Live cells + Dead cells)
